verdict.rationale: Notion documents its own agents, including chat sessions in which you converse with the Agent and approve actions. It also documents a first-party Notion MCP that lets AI clients such as Claude Code or Cursor search, read, create and update workspace content on a user's behalf, so natural-language operation of the product is clearly delivered. missing for 10: detailed first-party documentation of which in-app operations the Notion Agent can perform from natural-language commands, and independent or hands-on corroboration of how reliably it works.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Use sessions to start a chat, stream the Agent's reply, submit an action when needed, and read its event history.
Notion MCP lets an MCP client, such as Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex, connect to your Notion workspace through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
Read, create, and update Notion content.
You can maintain it yourself or ask an assistant to do it for you.
